Q3 - Tobacco Reporter

    Tag: Q3  

  The company continues to move forward with plans to expand its nicotine pouch business through a joint acquisition of Another Snus Factory with Altria by year-end.

  Reflecting strong performance, JT raised its full-year forecasts across all metrics, projecting a 13.1% rise in revenue and a 24.3% increase in adjusted operating profit at constant FX. CEO Masamichi Terabatake credited growth in the Ploom heated tobacco segment, with Ploom AURA and EVO premium sticks boosting Japan’s HTS market share to 15.5%. JT also announced a revised annual dividend of ¥234 ($1.52) per share, up ¥26 ($0.17), in line with record-high earnings and its shareholder return policy.

  Participants should call at least 10 minutes in advance and follow the audio prompts to register. The call will also be broadcast live as a listen-only webcast from the investor relations section of the companys website . The replay of the webcast will be available on the site two hours following the call.

  PMI’s smoke-free portfolio continued to expand rapidly, now accounting for 41% of total net revenues and 42% of gross profit. Volumes of smoke-free products rose 16.6%, led by the IQOS heated tobacco line and ZYN nicotine pouches. IQOS strengthened its market share across Europe and Asia, while ZYN’s U.S. offtake surged 39% following its return to full availability. The e-vapor brand VEEV also posted a 91% jump in shipments, solidifying PMI’s diversified presence across smoke-free categories.

  Reflecting this momentum, PMI raised its full-year adjusted EPS guidance and boosted its quarterly dividend by 8.9% to $1.47 per share. CEO Jacek Olczak said the company’s smoke-free business “continues to outgrow the industry by a clear margin,” adding that PMI is “on track to exceed” its 2024–2026 growth targets.

Domestic cigarette and MST volumes are declining. Management attributes that to industry declines, pressure on adult nicotine consumers' discretionary income, and a move to e-vapor. The growth is in nicotine pouches. on! PLUS has expanded to 120,000 stores. Management says the industry's cigarette decline has moderated for four straight quarters, and CEO Sal Mancuso pointed to the crackdown on illicit vapes: "We believe increased enforcement activity, including supply-related disruptions at the border, is helping slow demand for illicit products." Second-quarter 2026 net revenues were $6.11 billion, up 0.1% from a year earlier. Adjusted EPS rose 2.8% to $1.48. Over the twelve months to June 30, 2026, Altria's dividend ate up a manageable 78% of free cash flow, in line with the 74.6% to 82.0% range from fiscal 2021 to fiscal 2025. **Altria Group reported resilient third-quarter 2026 results, supported by pricing in its smokeable products business, continued growth in nicotine pouches and higher earnings per share. The company also raised its full-year earnings guidance.**

Third-quarter net revenues increased 1.0% to USD 6.13 billion, while revenues net of excise taxes rose 3.6% to USD 5.44 billion. Reported diluted EPS grew 7.1% to USD 1.51. For the first nine months of 2026, net revenues increased 1.4% to USD 17.7 billion, while reported diluted EPS advanced 21.2% to USD 4.18.

CEO Sal Mancuso said: “Altria delivered strong financial performance in the third quarter, growing adjusted diluted earnings per share by 4.8%, while continuing to invest in our Vision and building on our foundation for the future.” He added that Cowboy Cut continued to strengthen the premium positioning of Marlboro, while Basic gained further traction in the discount segment.

The smokeable products segment remained Altria’s key earnings contributor. Segment net revenues increased 0.8% to USD 5.43 billion, while reported operating companies income (OCI) rose 3.8% to USD 3.05 billion, driven primarily by higher pricing.

Domestic cigarette shipment volume declined 2.9% to 15.7 billion sticks during the quarter. Marlboro shipments fell 6.4% to 13.3 billion cigarettes, although the brand maintained a 39.5% retail share of the U.S. cigarette market and increased its share of the premium segment to 60.0%.

In oral tobacco, net revenues were broadly stable at USD 688 million, while OCI declined due to lower shipment volumes and increased promotional spending. Total oral tobacco shipment volume decreased 4.3% to 170.6 million cans. However, nicotine pouch brand on! continued to grow, with shipment volume rising 13.3% to 47.8 million cans.

**Altria Group (NYSE: MO)** met adjusted earnings expectations in Q3 while delivering a revenue beat that caught investors’ attention. The EPS forecast represents the midpoint of an $1.48 to $1.53 range among 11 analysts covering the stock, while revenue estimates span $5.23B to $5.37B.
